messages:
eric_support: Heads-up — Acme support ticket #12345. Customer reports clients disconnect mid-stream when they switch from LTE -> WiFi. App sees partial JSON chunk then socket closes. Server logs show 499/EOF and a bunch of `upstream reset` entries. Any ideas?

maria_sre: Thanks Eric. Do we have a sample connection id / trace id from the customer? Also which SDK & token TTL are they using? Usually this smells like NAT timeout or token refresh race.

eric_support: Sent trace id via DM: trace=acme-7f9c. App uses RN SDK v1.4.2, token TTL set to 30s (they refresh on app foreground). Customer says it reproduces ~80% when switching carriers or toggling hotspot.

maria_sre: 30s TTL is pretty short. If token refresh fires while SSE is mid-stream, some clients tear down and re-open causing partial output. Can you ask them to reproduce with TTL=300s to rule that out?

jordan_devex: Also confirm client reconnection/backoff logic. If they do a straight socket.close() on refresh rather than a graceful reconnect with resume, they'll lose partial chunk. What client code are they using? EventSource? fetch + ReadableStream?

eric_support: They shared snippet:
```js
const s = new EventSource(url + '?token=' + token);
s.onmessage = (e) => handleChunk(e.data);
// on token refresh they call s.close() then new EventSource
```
They say behavior: on mobile handoff, browser sometimes never reconnects and partial JSON becomes invalid.

maria_sre: Okay. Two action items: 1) Ask them to keep the token stable across handoffs (increase TTL) to see if token rotation is the trigger. 2) Have them enable client-level keepalive (send a 1s ping every ~15s) and set server-side heartbeat. On our side we can also enable debug SSE traces for trace=acme-7f9c.

eric_support: I asked them to reproduce with TTL=300 and to add keepalive. They replied with a short server log excerpt: 
```
[2026-03-15T18:02:13Z] conn=acme-7f9c recv: chunk(512) partial_json
[2026-03-15T18:02:14Z] conn=acme-7f9c upstream reset by peer
[2026-03-15T18:02:14Z] conn=acme-7f9c close 499 client closed request
```
They also attached a Chrome network capture showing a TCP RST around the switch.

jordan_devex: TCP RST during carrier handoff tracks with mobile NAT behavior. If the carrier drops the socket the client will see incomplete message. Best practice: client should buffer and validate JSON chunks and attempt resume. We don't currently offer chunk-resume semantics for EventSource — need durable session IDs to resume.

maria_sre: Short term checklist for Support: 1) Confirm TTL increase effect. 2) Recommend client exponential backoff + retry with idempotency key. 3) Enable short server heartbeat (every 15s) to keep NAT pinhole alive. 4) Collect a full server-side debug trace (I've flagged trace=acme-7f9c, request logs are being pulled, INC-2026-78).

eric_support: Customer tried TTL=300 and saw fewer failures but still some disconnects during fast hotspot toggles. They enabled keepalive and reported improved stability. They want to know if we can do server-side buffering to avoid partial JSON on abrupt disconnects.

jordan_devex: We can propose two approaches: 1) Server-side: emit smaller, self-contained events (avoid splitting JSON across chunks). 2) Protocol: switch from raw SSE to a resumable WebSocket/HTTP2 stream with resume tokens — longer-term. For now recommend application-level idempotent events and small chunk sizes.

maria_sre: I'll update the runbook: add guidance for mobile handoffs, suggest token TTL >= 300s for background/hand-off heavy apps, heartbeat <= 20s, and client buffering/validation. I'll attach the debug logs to INC-2026-78.

eric_support: Customer happy with the mitigation suggestions. They asked whether billing or auth errors could surface similarly — they saw a 401 once during one of the reconnects.

maria_sre: 401 on reconnect is almost always token expired or refresh endpoint returning 401. Recommend: pre-warm token refresh before expiry and if you must rotate mid-stream, do it via a handshake that doesn't require complete socket teardown. We'll add a troubleshooting note in Support KB.

eric_support: Great — I'll close the loop with Acme and add notes to the ticket. Thanks all :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Incident INC-2026-78 status updated: logs attached by maria_sre.
